extracted_concepts.name: Homogeneous Second-Order ODEs
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Linear differential equations with zero right-hand side and constant coefficients.

extracted_concepts.name: Characteristic Equation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Algebraic equation derived from homogeneous linear ODEs whose roots determine solution forms.

extracted_concepts.name: Method of Undetermined Coefficients
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Technique to find particular solutions by guessing a form matching the nonhomogeneous term.

extracted_concepts.name: Variation of Parameters
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: General method for finding particular solutions using variable coefficients applied to homogeneous solutions.

extracted_concepts.name: Spring-Mass System
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Mechanical model describing oscillatory motion governed by second-order linear ODEs.

extracted_concepts.name: Simple Harmonic Motion
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Oscillatory motion without damping or external forcing, characterized by constant amplitude.

extracted_concepts.name: Damped Oscillation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Motion where energy dissipates over time, causing amplitude to decrease exponentially.

extracted_concepts.name: Forced Oscillation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: System subjected to an external time-dependent driving force.

extracted_concepts.name: Resonance
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Phenomenon occurring when driving frequency approximately equals natural frequency, maximizing amplitude.

extracted_concepts.name: RLC Circuit
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Electrical circuit analogous to spring-mass systems, modeling charge dynamics with inductance, resistance, and capacitance.

extracted_concepts.name: First-Order ODE System
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Set of coupled first-order differential equations represented in matrix form.

extracted_concepts.name: Eigenvalue Method
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Technique solving linear ODE systems by decomposing the coefficient matrix into eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

extracted_concepts.name: Eigenvalues
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Scalar factors by which eigenvectors are scaled; determine qualitative stability behavior of linear systems.

extracted_concepts.name: Eigenvectors
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Nonzero vectors that remain parallel to themselves under linear transformation defined by the coefficient matrix.

extracted_concepts.name: Matrix Exponential
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Operator providing the fundamental solution to linear first-order systems x'=Ax.

extracted_concepts.name: Wave Equation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Second-order PDE describing propagation of waves such as sound, light, and vibrations.

extracted_concepts.name: Heat Equation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Diffusion-type PDE modeling temperature distribution and heat flow over time.

extracted_concepts.name: Laplace Equation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Second-order PDE governing steady-state potentials and equilibrium configurations.

extracted_concepts.name: Separation of Variables
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Analytical technique reducing PDEs to ordinary differential equations by assuming product solutions.

extracted_concepts.name: Fourier Series
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Infinite sum of sines and cosines representing periodic functions, arising naturally from boundary value problems.

extracted_concepts.name: Orthogonal Eigenfunctions
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Set of eigenfunctions from separation of variables that form a complete basis for function expansion.

extracted_concepts.name: Partial Differential Equations
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Equations involving partial derivatives of multivariable functions, extending ODEs to higher dimensions.

extracted_concepts.name: Ordinary Differential Equations
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Equations involving derivatives of functions of a single independent variable.

extracted_concepts.name: Coefficient Matrix
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Constant matrix containing parameters that define the linear relationship between state variables in first-order systems.

extracted_concepts.name: Natural Frequency
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Intrinsic frequency at which a system oscillates when undisturbed by external forces.

extracted_relations.evidence: Characteristic equation ar²+br+c=0 is derived directly from ay''+by'+cy=0.
Roots of the characteristic polynomial correspond to eigenvalues determining solution exponents.
Particular solution construction relies on known homogeneous solutions y₁, y₂.
Constructs y*=u₁y₁+u₂y₂ using fundamental homogeneous solutions.
Undamped spring-mass models exhibit simple harmonic motion.
Damping introduces exponential decay to the mass-spring dynamics.
External force F(t) drives the spring-mass system.
Resonance occurs when driving frequency approximately equals natural frequency.
Comparison of driving and natural frequencies determines resonance conditions.
Electrical charge dynamics LQ''+RQ'+Q/C=E(t) are mathematically analogous to mechanical oscillators.
System x'=Ax is defined entirely by the constant coefficient matrix A.
Solution given explicitly as x=e^(At)x₀.
Used to solve linear systems x'=Ax by spectral decomposition.
Decomposition requires computing eigenvalues λ of the coefficient matrix.
General solution combines eigenvectors v scaled by exponential terms.
Spectral properties dictate qualitative behaviors like stable nodes, spirals, and saddles.
Classical hyperbolic PDE describing wave propagation.
Classical parabolic PDE modeling diffusion processes.
Classical elliptic PDE governing steady-state potentials.
Primary analytical technique applied to classical PDEs.
Reduces multivariable PDEs into decoupled single-variable ODEs.
Boundary conditions yield eigenfunctions that naturally expand into Fourier series.
Series coefficients project onto a complete orthogonal system of eigenfunctions.
PDEs extend ODE theory to functions of multiple independent variables.
Eigenvalues are computed directly from the determinant of the coefficient matrix.
